metaDescription: Six compact snow blowers and powered shovels compared, 12 to 21 inches wide, for small drives, steps and tight storage, corded and cordless.
expertTake: The EGO SNT2122 is the strongest small machine if you want a real blower, and the Westinghouse WSnow20 is the sensible corded option for a short paved drive. The EGO SNS1201 and VOLTASK are shovel-class tools for steps and walks. Skip all of them if your drive is long or your snow routinely arrives knee-deep. Measure your narrowest path before you order. A shovel and a small blower together cover almost every small property. Check how many batteries are in the box before you pay.
introParagraphs: A small machine suits a short drive, a few steps and a garage with no room to spare. It trades width, depth and throw for a lighter body and an easier life in storage. The best small machine is the one you will actually take out of the shed in January.

Small covers two quite different tool types. Compact walk-behind blowers roll on wheels and clear a drive in a few passes, while shovel-class tools are carried and clear narrow strips. Deciding which type fits your property is the main choice before price or brand. Reading the box contents before ordering avoids the most common surprise. A short test pass on the first snowfall tells you more than any spec sheet.

products.name: EGO Power+ SNT2122 21-inch single-stage, 2 x 4Ah
products.description:
The SNT2122 is the most capable small blower in this group, a single-stage with a 21-inch path, a 180-degree chute and variable auger speed. Two 4Ah packs are rated for roughly a 10-car driveway in 8 inches of snow.

Variable speed is a genuine runtime lever: slow the auger for light snow, open it up for heavy. Against the 16-inch Greenworks it is wider and stronger, and against the 12-inch EGO shovel it is a different class of tool.

Packs are shared with EGO mowers and trimmers, so existing owners save. Keep it on paved surfaces and store the packs indoors. If your drive is longer than about three cars, add a second set of packs or step up to the 24-inch two-stage. It is the one to buy if you want a single machine for a small house and a garden.
products.bestFor: Short to medium paved drives wanting a real blower in a compact frame.
pros: Two packs and a charger in the kit
cons: Smaller packs limit a long drive

products.name: Westinghouse WSnow20 20-inch corded blower, steel auger
products.description:
The WSnow20 is a compact corded machine with a rubber-tipped steel auger, a 20-inch path and a stated 680 pounds per minute. It has dual LED lights and 7-inch snow-grabbing wheels.

A corded design means no battery cost and no charging, and the lightest frame of the full-size machines. The limit is the cord, which reaches only as far as your extension.

Against the DEKOPRO 18-inch it is slightly wider and has a steel auger. Keep the cord behind you and inspect the rubber tips each season. Most owners use it at the lower end of its cord reach, so buy a heavy-gauge extension cord rather than reuse a thin one. Its compact frame also makes it easier to put into a car for a second property.
products.bestFor: Short paved drives close to an outlet.
pros: Steel auger at a compact size

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-inch brushless snow blower, tool only
products.description:
This is a 16-inch 40V brushless single-stage that clears snow up to 10 inches deep and throws about 25 feet. The listing is tool only, so the battery and charger are extra.

The narrow body is the point. A 16-inch machine fits through a side gate, along a sidewalk and into a corner of a shed. It is a good fit if you already own 40V packs from a mower or trimmer.

If you do not own a pack, price a kit before buying, since the battery is the main cost. If you have no 40V pack, price a kit from the same family before buying the bare tool, since the pack is the main cost.
products.bestFor: Owners with 40V packs who want a narrow machine.

products.name: VOLTASK 24V 13.2-inch cordless snow shovel, 4Ah
products.description:
The VOLTASK is a 24V cordless shovel that clears a path about 13 inches wide and throws snow up to 23 feet. A 24V 4Ah battery is rated for about 30 minutes of continuous runtime.

It is light enough to carry up steps and across a deck, and the ergonomic handle reduces strain. Against the EGO SNS1201 shovel it offers a longer stated runtime but a less established platform.

Use it for light snow and short walks. For a driveway, step up to a wheeled blower. Because it is carried, expect to feel the weight after twenty minutes; take breaks and clear in thin layers. It makes sense as a second tool alongside a bigger machine.

products.name: DEKOPRO 18-inch corded electric snow blower, 15A
products.description:
The DEKOPRO is an 18-inch corded blower with a two-blade steel auger, a 9-inch depth and a stated 800 pounds per minute. It throws up to 25 feet and the chute rotates 180 degrees.

At 18 inches it is the narrowest corded machine here, which is useful on a short drive. Against the WSnow20 it gives up 2 inches of width but also has a steel auger.

It suits a small drive with an outlet close by. Plug it into a ground-fault outlet and keep the plug off wet snow with a cord clip on the handle.
products.bestFor: Small paved drives near an outlet.

products.name: EGO Power+ SNS1201 12-inch cordless snow shovel, 2.5Ah
products.description:
The SNS1201 is a light 12-inch shovel with a dial that sets the chute direction over a 60-degree range. One 2.5Ah pack is rated for about a 3-car driveway in 6 inches of snow.

Its value lies in being on the EGO ARC platform, so it can use bigger packs for longer runs. Against the VOLTASK it has a shorter stated runtime out of the box but a deeper platform.

Treat it as the tool for steps and the front walk. If you later buy a bigger EGO machine, the same packs will power both, which makes it a low-risk first purchase. Treat it as a quick-reaction tool by the door.
products.bestFor: Steps and porches for owners on the EGO platform.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The EGO SNT2122, WSnow20 and DEKOPRO are wheeled blowers that clear 18 to 21 inches wide. The VOLTASK and SNS1201 are shovel-class tools clearing 12 to 13 inches. A blower suits a drive; a shovel suits steps and short walks. Measure the narrowest gate on your route before choosing a width; a 21-inch body will not pass a 20-inch gate. A small machine that is too narrow for the job wastes time, while one that is too wide wastes storage, so match width to the actual drive and gate. Count your passes: a ten-foot walk takes six passes at 20 inches but nine at 13.

Compact machines run from 12 to 21 inches. Narrower paths fit gates and sidewalks, while 20 inches or more saves passes on a drive. A rule of thumb is to match the tool to the longest continuous run you make, not the average clear. Corded saves the cost of a battery but costs you the time to move the cord, and the cord is the first thing to wear out. Cordless costs more but lets you clear the whole property in one trip, which is why it suits drives away from an outlet.

Corded models like the WSnow20 and DEKOPRO need an outlet but never run out. Cordless models like the SNT2122 and VOLTASK roam freely but run 20 to 30 minutes. An outlet within easy reach of the whole drive makes corded the best value; if not, go cordless. Small tools earn their keep by being easy to reach for. If the machine lives behind a car or under a shelf, it will not get used for a dusting, and a light powered shovel hanging by the door will.

A small machine should be easy to lift and store. The shovels hang on a hook; the blowers need a corner of the garage. Check the storage spot before buying; a 20-inch blower needs a footprint about the size of a bicycle. A stated depth of 9 or 10 inches is a ceiling for light snow. Wet snow weighs several times more per inch, so a small motor stalls well before the ceiling.

The Greenworks clears 10 inches and the DEKOPRO 9. Deeper snow means a layered approach or a bigger machine. Treat stated depths as ceilings and clear deeper snow in layers from the top down. Look at the box contents first: some listings are tool only, which is the cheapest way in if you own packs and the most expensive if you do not.

If you own EGO or Greenworks packs, the matching machine saves the cost of a battery. A tool-only listing is a trap if you do not own a pack. If you own no cordless tools, a kit with batteries included is usually the right start. Platform lock-in is the long-term cost. An EGO or Greenworks pack bought for the blower will power the mower, trimmer and hedge cutter, which is why the platform matters more than the machine.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tool class
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated wheeled blowers from shovel-class tools. The class decides how much ground each can cover. Class is the first filter because a shovel cannot do a blower's work. That is why the SNT2122 and the SNS1201 sit in different roles despite sharing a battery.

howWeEvaluated.title: Width and depth
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared widths of 12 to 21 inches and depths of 9 to 10 inches where listed. A wider path is not always better in a small yard. We counted passes on a typical short drive to compare widths. Narrower machines pass through gates that wider ones cannot.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power source
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared corded and cordless models. Cordless adds pack care; corded adds a cord. Corded runtime is unlimited but the cord is a constraint. We used stated runtimes only as relative figures.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns, we weighed storage, pack care and paddle wear. Small machines should be easy to live with, so we weighed lifting and storage heavily. A tool that is awkward to store is a tool that does not get used.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit to property
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each tool to a small drive, walk or steps. This is an editorial assessment, not a measured score. We recommend buying for the worst storm you expect, not the average. This is an editorial assessment, not a measured score.

maintenance.why: Cold reduces output. A warm closet beats a cold garage. Rotate packs so they age evenly.
A damaged cord is a shock risk. Check the section near the plug first. Store the cord loosely coiled.
Rubber tips wear. Replace paddles when they stop touching the pavement. Replace paddles in pairs.
Slush freezes overnight. A dry rag takes under a minute. Dry the chute before storing.
Unplug or remove the battery first. Wait for the auger to stop turning first. Never put a hand near the auger. Wait for the auger to stop before reaching in.

faq.q: What counts as a small snow blower?
faq.a: Usually a machine under 22 inches wide or a powered shovel. These suit short drives and walks. Machines under 22 inches wide are the sweet spot for these properties. Choose a width that fits your narrowest gate first, then your drive.

faq.q: Corded or cordless for a small drive?
faq.a: Corded runs all day near an outlet. Cordless roams freely but runs 20 to 30 minutes. Owners with both often keep a corded unit for the drive and a cordless shovel for steps. If you have only one outlet, a long thin cord will not do; buy a heavy-gauge cord.

faq.q: Can a shovel clear a driveway?
faq.a: Only a short one, slowly. A wheeled blower is better. A shovel is best kept for steps and the front walk. Take breaks to rest your arms.
No. Single-stage augers throw stones. Clear the paved part with the blower and shovel the stones. Gravel is the single biggest reason to avoid a single-stage machine.

faq.q: Is a small machine enough for deep snow?
faq.a: Not above about 8 to 10 inches. Clear in layers or use a bigger machine. Layers of 4 to 6 inches work best for small machines. If your area gets deep snow often, a larger machine is the better buy.
Hang shovels on a hook and keep batteries indoors. A wall hook for a shovel frees floor space. Keep batteries indoors. Bring batteries inside well before the first freeze.
